map.计算权重向量的 L1 与 L2 范数。: Compute the L1 and L2 norms of a weight vector.
map.两个范数量化权重矩阵的整体规模：L1 反映绝对值总量，对少量大权重敏感；L2（F: The two norms quantify the overall scale of the weight matrix: L1 reflects total absolute value, sensitive to a few large weights; L2 (Frobenius norm) reflects energy and is often written directly into the loss as a penalty. Monitoring the norm over training quickly reveals weight explosion.
map.L1 倾向稀疏，L2 倾向小权重。: L1 tends to sparsity, L2 tends to small weights.
map.L1 范数 ‖w‖₁=Σ|wᵢ|，L2 范数 ‖w‖₂=√(Σwᵢ²)，分别衡量: L1 norm ‖w‖₁ = Σ|wᵢ|, L2 norm ‖w‖₂ = √(Σwᵢ²), each measuring weight magnitude.
map.对应惩罚项 λ‖w‖₁(Lasso,促稀疏)与 (λ/2)‖w‖₂²(Ridge: The corresponding penalties are λ‖w‖₁ (Lasso, sparse) and (λ/2)‖w‖₂² (Ridge, smooth).

map.w=[3,−4]：‖w‖₁=|3|+|−4|=7；‖w‖₂=√(9+16)=5，: w=[3,-4]: ‖w‖₁ = |3|+|-4| = 7; ‖w‖₂ = √(9+16) = 5, L2 penalty = (λ/2)·25. L1 penalizes large weights equally, L2 presses large weights harder.
map.L1 在零点不可导、等高线为菱形，最优解易落在坐标轴上使部分权重恰为 0，实现特: L1 is non-differentiable at zero with diamond contours, so the optimum tends to land on axes, zeroing some weights and achieving feature selection; L2 only shrinks, never zeroes.
map.正则系数 λ 怎么选？: How to choose the regularization coefficient λ?
map.用验证集网格/贝叶斯搜索；λ 过小过拟合、过大欠拟合。通常对权重先标准化，再在: Use grid or Bayesian search on the validation set; too small λ overfits, too large underfits. Usually standardize weights first, then scan λ in the 10⁻⁴ to 10 range.
map.L1/L2 范数（本页代码口径，四个权重 w1–w4）：L1=|w1|+|w2|: L1/L2 norms (this page's code, four weights w1–w4): L1=|w1|+|w2|+|w3|+|w4|; L2=√(w1²+w2²+w3²+w4²), both kept to 3 decimals. Validation: no strict checks; empty values count as 0. Grading: no fixed tiers; the norms grow monotonically with the absolute weights, and with all weights zero both L1 and L2 are 0.
map.判读与对照（本页代码口径，与上方公式互补）：由范数不等式恒有 L1≥L2，等号仅: Interpretation and comparison (this page's code, complementary to the formula above): the norm inequality guarantees L1≥L2, with equality only when at most one weight is non-zero; multiplying all weights by c multiplies both norms by |c| (degree-one homogeneity); the comparison chart plots |w| and w² per weight — w² is smaller when |w|<1 and larger when |w|>1, showing intuitively that L1 is dominated by large weights while L2 relatively suppresses their contribution. Validation: shares the same inputs as above. Grading: no fixed tiers.
